articles.title: Rochdale AFC Confirms EFL Trophy Fixtures for 2026 Season
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC has announced its fixtures for the EFL Trophy, detailing the matches scheduled for the upcoming season. Fans can look forward to an exciting series of games.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC has confirmed its fixtures for the EFL Trophy, with details of matches scheduled for the 2026 season. The announcement was made on August 19, 2026, via the club's official website.

The EFL Trophy features teams from League One and League Two, providing clubs with a chance to compete for silverware. Rochdale aims to make a strong impression in this year's tournament.

Fans should check the club's website for specific match dates, times, and ticketing information. The fixtures promise to deliver exciting football at Spotland Stadium.

As the season progresses, supporters can expect updates on match results and player performances, contributing to the club's journey in the EFL Trophy.

articles.title: NHS Staff at Rochdale Infirmary to Strike Over Overtime Pay Dispute
articles.excerpt: More than 350 staff at Rochdale Infirmary and three other Greater Manchester hospitals will strike for three days next week due to a dispute over overtime payments, following the withdrawal of a payment offer by Northern Care Alliance.
articles.content_html:
More than 350 employees of the Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust (NCA), including nurses and clinical support workers at Rochdale Infirmary, will strike for three days next week. The strike is scheduled for Monday 24th, Wednesday 26th, and Friday 28th August, in response to a dispute regarding overtime payments.

The dispute arose after NCA management withdrew an offer intended to resolve the issue before discussions could take place. The conflict centres on the trust's use of NHS Professionals (NHSP) to manage overtime, which has reportedly resulted in staff earning less than their normal pay rates during overtime shifts. According to UNISON, some staff members are missing out on more than £80 per shift due to this arrangement.

Kevin Dolan, a regional organiser for UNISON, expressed frustration over the situation, stating that NCA leadership has shown a lack of commitment to resolving the issue. He emphasised that staff are merely seeking to receive what their contracts entitle them to, and he called for continued negotiations.

In addition to the strikes, staff from all four affected hospitals, including Rochdale Infirmary, Royal Oldham Hospital, Fairfield Hospital in Bury, and Salford Royal Hospital, will gather in Salford on Wednesday 26th August for a unified day of protest. The outcome of these actions could significantly impact NHS services in the region, particularly in operating theatres.

articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Derker Tram Stop
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers. Step-free access is available via alternative routes until further notice.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop has been out of service since 8:09pm on 18 August 2026, impacting passengers using the tram service. There is currently no confirmed date for when the lift will be restored.

For customers travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading towards Rochdale can also use a ramp from Cromford Street, followed by a track crossing to access the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester has apologised for any inconvenience caused by this disruption and is advising passengers to plan their journeys accordingly. Passengers are encouraged to check the latest travel alerts on the Transport for Greater Manchester website for ongoing updates regarding the lift's status and any other travel disruptions.

Further information can be found on the Transport for Greater Manchester website, where live travel alerts are regularly updated.
